components.css: .ds-shell{overflow:hidden;border:1px solid var(--border-strong,rgba(235,237,249,.18));border-radius:16px;background:var(--surface,#1d1f2c);color:var(--text,#ebedf9);box-shadow:0 24px 60px rgba(8,9,16,.45);font-family:ui-monospace,SFMono-Regular,JetBrains Mono,Menlo,Consolas,monospace}.ds-shell-bar{display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:space-between;gap:.8rem;padding:.6rem .85rem;border-bottom:1px solid var(--border,rgba(235,237,249,.1));background:color-mix(in srgb,var(--surface,#1d1f2c) 70%,var(--bg,#14151f));font-size:.78rem;color:var(--muted,#8789a4)}.ds-shell-bar button{flex:0 0 auto;padding:.25rem .6rem;border:1px solid var(--border-strong,rgba(235,237,249,.18));border-radius:7px;background:transparent;color:var(--text-2,#b7bace)}.ds-shell pre{margin:0;padding:1.1rem 1.2rem 1.3rem;font-size:.86rem;line-height:1.85;overflow-x:auto}.ds-shell span{display:block}.ds-shell b,.ds-shell em{color:var(--accent,#cf6242);font-style:normal}.ds-shell .ds-dim{color:var(--muted,#8789a4)}.ds-sr-only{position:absolute;width:1px;height:1px;padding:0;margin:-1px;overflow:hidden;clip:rect(0,0,0,0);white-space:nowrap;border:0}

components.name: Overlay Stack
components.description: A bolder hero-only artifact that makes source, worktree, restore state, and git exclusion feel physical behind the shell panel.
components.css: .ds-overlay-stack{position:relative;isolation:isolate;min-height:13rem}.ds-overlay-stack:before{content:"";position:absolute;inset:22% 0 8% 18%;border-radius:22px;background:color-mix(in srgb,var(--accent,#cf6242) 86%,var(--accent-2,#aa462c));transform:rotate(2.4deg);z-index:-1}.ds-overlay-stack span{position:absolute;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:.18rem;min-width:min(11rem,100%);padding:.7rem .82rem;border:1px solid var(--border-strong,rgba(235,237,249,.18));border-radius:12px;background:color-mix(in srgb,var(--surface,#1d1f2c) 88%,var(--bg,#14151f));color:var(--text,#ebedf9)}.ds-overlay-stack span:nth-child(1){top:.2rem;left:-.75rem;transform:rotate(-4deg)}.ds-overlay-stack span:nth-child(2){right:-.35rem;bottom:.5rem;transform:rotate(3deg)}.ds-overlay-stack span:nth-child(3){top:-.3rem;right:4.5rem;transform:rotate(1.5deg)}.ds-overlay-stack b{color:var(--muted,#8789a4);font:700 .74rem/1.2 Metropolis,system-ui,sans-serif}.ds-overlay-stack code{color:var(--text,#ebedf9);font:400 .78rem/1.2 ui-monospace,SFMono-Regular,JetBrains Mono,Menlo,Consolas,monospace;overflow-wrap:anywhere;white-space:normal}@media (forced-colors:active){.ds-overlay-stack{display:none}}

narrative.overview:
repoverlay's visual system should feel like the bench where a developer keeps the tools they trust: close at hand, clearly labeled, and built for repeatable work. The current site uses a dark technical surface, a clay-orange accent, and compact command examples to make invisible git mechanics feel tangible rather than abstract.

The system is brand-first because the primary frontend surface is a docs and landing site, but it should not perform like a generic marketing page. It rejects floating SaaS dashboards, hero metrics, ornamental gradient-card grids, and vague productivity copy. The design earns trust by showing concrete files, commands, exclusions, and restore flows.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-by-default developer environment with a complete light-mode counterpart.
Metropolis-driven type system: wide, sturdy, and readable rather than trendy.
Clay-orange accent used as a working signal for action, success-path emphasis, and command prompts.
Tonal layering, borders, and a single structural shell shadow instead of decorative depth.
Real workflow objects as imagery: command panels, config file names, overlay flow steps, and stacked source/worktree/exclude artifacts.

rules.name: The One-Tool Accent Rule
rules.body: Clay is the only brand accent. Do not introduce blue, purple, or rainbow developer-tool gradients unless the product itself gains a new semantic state that requires them.

rules.name: The No Cream Rule
rules.body: Light mode stays cool and neutral. Warmth comes from the clay accent, not from sand, bone, parchment, or ivory backgrounds.

rules.name: The Mono Earns Its Place Rule
rules.body: Monospace appears only when the content is literally code, commands, file paths, or terminal output. Do not use monospace as a generic technical decoration.

rules.name: The Flat-Until-Physical Rule
rules.body: A surface gets a shadow only when it is meant to read as a physical object. Ordinary feature cells stay flat and use borders plus tonal contrast.

rules.name: The No Silent Failure Rule
rules.body: Interactive utilities must surface failure states. The homepage copy button announces copied and failed states, and release text is sourced from build-time Cargo metadata.

dos: Do show real workflow objects: `.git/info/exclude`, `repoverlay apply`, `repoverlay restore`, overlay state, and file paths.
Do keep Clay rare enough to remain meaningful; use it for actions, prompts, release markers, and the most important command artifact.
Do use the existing 16px container radius and 7-10px utility radii before inventing new shape values.
Do keep text contrast strong in both color schemes, especially secondary prose on tinted dark surfaces.
Do make reduced-motion behavior visible and complete; content must be readable before any animation enhancement runs.
donts: Don't make repoverlay look like a generic SaaS landing page with gradient cards, hero metrics, floating dashboard mockups, or vague productivity promises.
Don't use terminal-only hacker cosplay. Commands are evidence, not a whole aesthetic.
Don't add overly playful mascots or decorative AI-assistant tropes.
Don't use gradient text, colored side-stripe borders, nested glass cards, or repeated uppercase eyebrows above every section.
Don't replace the cool light-mode palette with cream, sand, parchment, bone, ivory, or other warm-neutral defaults.
